descriptions.description:
Dimensional Human Field Theory (DHFT) identifies a closed explanatory architecture. The Dimensional Human Physics (DHP) spine specifies lawful
mechanics of load, constraint, accumulation, movement, and time. The present
paper provides the first minimal nonlinear dynamical formalization consistent with that spine. A three-variable structural system is specified comprising
capacity C(t), boundary permeability B(t), and effective load L(t). Instability is governed by a stability margin κ(C,B) determined by the interaction of structural
capacity and boundary integrity. Load accumulation occurs when input exceeds the system’s dissipation capacity. As structural parameters drift through capacity erosion, boundary degradation, or sustained load accumulation, the equilibrium manifold may undergo a foldn(saddle-node) bifurcation. Near criticality the system reduces locally to the
canonical saddle-node normal form. The resulting system exhibits fold bifurcation structure and hysteresis as a geometric consequence. The framework remains substrate-agnostic: heterogeneous stressors may project into the load
variable without altering structural invariants. The result is a minimal stability geometry capable of modeling threshold transitions across multiple empirical domains while preserving the architectural closure of DHFT.

https://zenodo.org/records/19076075

Full DHFT Formal System Repository: https://osf.io/9psmd/

Falsifiability and Failure Conditions

DHFT is falsified only if its governing structural relations fail—specifically, if load under constraint does not produce instability or reorganization, if interpretation alone alters system behavior, if propagation fails under coupling, or if projection violates structural invariance.
DHFT does not model subjective experience (thought, emotion, perception) as variables; dimensionality refers to structural degrees of freedom in system dynamics, not experiential or psychological dimensions.

Within DHFT, Dimensional Human Physics (DHP) defines the lawful structural mechanics of load, capacity, and boundary conditions. Despite its name, “physics” refers to structural mechanics rather than material or biological processes.

DHFT is stewarded by the Somatic Rising Institute, founded by Cara Tonucci. 

Somatic Rising Institute (SRI): 
www.somaticrisinginstitute.org
